category_title: Students without MHD who engage in exclusionary behaviors like imitation or insults
scenario_title: Addressing exclusionary behaviors and insults towards peers with MHD
minimal_context: The student is discussing a recent classroom interaction with the teacher to learn how to coexist with classmates who have mental health disorders.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: I want to talk about what happened during the group activity today. I noticed there was some trouble.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Yeah, there was some trouble between some kids in my class because of insults. Alex was being disruptive and ruining our game.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What did you and the other kids do when that happened?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Well, in our school there are kids with disorders, and when he started acting weird, some other kids imitated him. If I did that, I would be punished!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Why do you think the other kids were imitating him?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Because it's not fair! If I acted like him, I'd be punished. I know sometimes people can be really horrible to them and they can’t defend themselves on their own, but I'm going to keep insulting and imitating him until he gets in trouble too.

task.content: Interacting and coexisting with classmates who have mental health disorders (MHD) in an inclusive classroom setting
task.learning_goal: Understand that diversity is the norm and that around them there are people with varying personal characteristics with which they all had to coexist as equals

context.environment: Spanish public primary school that has an inclusive pedagogical project
context.social_setting: Groups that have children with SEN and peers without MHD

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When there is a difference which becomes disruptive and needs some kind of containment
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Insulting and imitating classmates with disorders, and being really horrible to them
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Believing that similar behaviours would be punished without further explanation, since they would have no supposed mental disorder behind them to explain or justify them

behavior_patterns.condition: When interacting with peers who have disorders
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Imitating them and directing insults at them, causing trouble between kids in the class
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Lacking understanding of the peers' disruptive behaviors and problems
